messages:
maria_support: Customer reported a large billing spike after upgrading the Python SDK to 1.31. They say a bunch of requests started failing with 401, the client retried aggressively, and token usage spiked. Pasting their logs and repro below.

maria_support: CUSTOMER LOGS:
```
2026-03-02T14:12:03Z POST /v1/generate 401 Unauthorized
2026-03-02T14:12:03Z redwood.client.retry Retrying request (attempt=1)
2026-03-02T14:12:04Z POST /v1/generate 401 Unauthorized
2026-03-02T14:12:04Z redwood.client.retry Retrying request (attempt=2)
2026-03-02T14:12:06Z POST /v1/generate 200 OK
```

maria_support: Repro steps customer provided:
```python
# pip install redwood==1.31
from redwood import Client
# previously they passed `credential_chain=None` to opt-out of automatic chain; code used to work
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv("RW_KEY"), credential_chain=None)
resp = client.generate("hello")
```

jamie_eng: Thanks — can you confirm the exact SDK package name and the full install output? I want to see if a transitive changed dep could have altered retry defaults.

maria_support: They sent `redwood==1.31.0` and pip shows deps: httpx==0.25.0, backoff==2.2.0. They said removing `credential_chain=None` in their init made it work again (i.e., using default flow).

jamie_eng: I think this is the bug. In 1.31 we removed `credential_chain` as a public kwarg (we migrated to `credentials` config) but forgot to add a compatibility alias. When users pass the old kwarg it silently falls into our new code path which triggers an immediate credential refresh+fallback. If that refresh hits our auth service and returns 401 briefly, our client-side retry loop (backoff settings) was more aggressive due to the httpx upgrade — leading to retry amplification and multiple successful token usages once refresh succeeded. That matches the customer's pattern.

jamie_eng: Short repro on my laptop: if you call Client(..., credential_chain=None) with 1.31 we do a noop-to-new-config mapping which sets `auto_refresh=True` accidentally. That causes an immediate refresh attempt. Patch idea: add a thin compatibility shim that maps `credential_chain=None` -> `credentials=LegacyChain(allow_opt_out=True)` and revert backoff defaults to the 1.30 behavior.

olivia_prodops: Can we get a mitigation customers can apply immediately? Pinning guidance please.

jamie_eng: Workaround: pin to 1.30 (pip install redwood==1.30.2) or explicitly construct the new config API: `Client(credentials=LocalCredentials(opt_out=True))`. But we need a one-line pin we can send to the affected accounts.

maria_support: I'll send the pin: `pip install 'redwood==1.30.2'` to affected customers and offer the explicit config snippet.

sre-oncall: We should also look for signs of auth service flapping at the same time. Tagging infra: any 401 spikes in frontdoor-auth logs for those org_ids between 14:10-14:20 UTC? Correlation IDs from customer: `corr=abc123` `req=def456`.

jamie_eng: Filed internal issue: GH #8342 (priv) — title: "py: restore credential_chain compatibility + revert aggressive retry defaults after httpx bump". Plan: release 1.31.1 that adds the alias + pins backoff to previous values, and 1.32 will be the breaking-change release with migration notes. ETA for 1.31.1: today EOD if QA green.

deploy-bot: created release branch `release/1.31.1` from main and opened PR #8347. CI started.

maria_support: Sending customer the temporary pin and apologizing. I'll offer to upgrade them to 1.31.1 when it's out and confirm we will credit obvious overages caused by our bug.

olivia_prodops: Please include a short rollback plan if 1.31.1 causes regressions — we should be able to revert quickly to 1.30.2 for affected orgs.

jamie_eng: Agreed. I'll keep this thread updated with CI/QA results. If anyone sees other similar threads, please tag me.

maria_support: Thanks — I'll mark this P1 and escalate billing cases to finance for potential credits. :pray:
